title: How much e-waste still comes into Thailand?

voiceover.text: Thailand banned electronic waste imports in twenty twenty. So how much still comes in, through customs?
We looked at U.N. Comtrade: the U.N. trade database, built from each country's customs records.
Until twenty fourteen, it was one to three tonnes of battery waste a year. In twenty fifteen, it doubled, to six and a half.
In January twenty sixteen, a military government order exempted some factories, including waste plants, from town-planning rules. By twenty nineteen, it had become four hundred and seven tonnes.
In September twenty twenty, Thailand's import ban took effect. That year: about two hundred forty tonnes.
The next year: three hundred thirty-five.
From twenty twenty-two, the customs codes got more detailed, so we can see every kind of e-waste.
And twenty twenty-five was the biggest year on record: over twelve hundred tonnes.
In June twenty twenty-five, the ban was expanded to these new codes. Yet over eleven hundred tonnes were declared in the second half of that year.
And in the first five months of twenty twenty-six: four hundred and nine tonnes. Eight times the same months of twenty twenty-five.
